title: Oil and talents (Matthew 25:1–30)
hookLine: a phone at two percent at midnight, ten lamps, and money buried out of fear
tomorrow: a throne, every nation, and the King asks about… sandwiches?

lines: TWO PERCENT, AND THE RIDE IS LATE.
cards: Phone at two percent, the ride is late, and the charger is at home, and the night keeps getting longer. Jesus tells that night.

Ten virgins, young women of a wedding party, wait with lamps for a bridegroom who is very late, and every one of them dozes off. At midnight, a cry: "Behold, the bridegroom cometh; go ye out to meet him."
They wake and trim their lamps, and five of them find they brought no oil to spare. Their lamps are going out.

teach.h: THEY ALL SLEPT; FIVE BROUGHT OIL.
teach.b: The five ask, "Give us of your oil; for our lamps are gone out." The others say there may not be enough for both: go and buy. While they're gone, the bridegroom comes and the door is shut.
Notice what wasn't the difference. They all slept. The wise weren't more awake.
They had simply brought oil. Some things can't be borrowed at midnight; they're carried in before the long wait. Then a second story.

A man going on a journey hands his servants his money, "to every man according to his several ability": five talents, two, and one. A talent here is a sum of money, the lord's money. Two servants trade and double it.
The third digs a hole and buries it.
When the master returns, the first two hear the same praise: "Well done, thou good and faithful servant: thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things."
Five or two, the same well done. The praise isn't for the size of the pile; it's for being faithful with what was in your hands.

teach.h: I WAS AFRAID, AND HID IT.
teach.b: Then the third: "I was afraid, and went and hid thy talent in the earth."
Fear kept the money perfectly safe, and did nothing with it. Two stories, one week: carry your oil in, and don't let fear bury what you were handed.

how: Christians draw on these two parables when they speak of being ready for Christ's return and of stewardship, using well what God has given; some churches read them in the weeks before Advent.

o: two offerings brought to the Temple at festivals
the lamp oil and coins sent with Jesus' disciples
two parables: oil for a long wait, money not buried

games.q: oil and talents — tap the pairs.
p: hid in the earth out of fear

s: the wise ones stayed awake while the foolish ones slept
they all slumbered and slept. the difference was the oil they'd brought.
in this story, a talent is a sum of money
the lord's money, handed out to every man according to his several ability.
the servant with two talents got less praise than the one with five
both hear: well done, thou good and faithful servant.

games.q: your mom starts a long season caring for your grandpa: months of hospital runs. by the parable of the lamps, what does she do now?
o: stock what keeps her lit: sleep, a friend to call, her prayers.
stay up every night, so she never once dozes off.
trust she'll find energy somehow when the hard night comes.
games.why: all ten slept, wise and foolish alike. the wise ones had brought oil. readiness is carried in before the long wait; it can't be borrowed at midnight.

practice: Name one thing in your hands right now that fear is tempting you to bury: a voice, an idea, a skill, a hard conversation. Name the fear in a few plain words, the way the third servant did: I was afraid.
Then choose one small way to use it this week, and hold that plan in mind while you breathe.

wordCard.voice: Oil and talents. Two stories in Matthew 25: lamps that need oil for a long wait, and money meant to be used, not buried.

orig.note: Greek for talent, in Matthew 25:15: in this story, a sum of money.

carryVoice: Your line: well done. The servant with two hears the same praise as the servant with five. Until tomorrow.
